## Positive product: match the signs {.psf-lesson .split-example}

Either order of the pair works. Here, putting the even coefficient first lets you take $2x$ out of the first group.

:::::: {.example-pair}

::::: {.model}

<h3>Worked example</h3>

$2x^2+7x+6$

::: {.fragment}

$P=12$, $S=7$: both positive.

:::

::: {.fragment}

| Pair | $1,\ 12$ | $2,\ 6$ | $3,\ 4$ |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| Sum | $13$ | $8$ | $7$ |

:::

::: {.fragment}

Choose $3,4$: $3+4=7$.

:::

::: {.fragment}

$=2x^2+4x+3x+6$

:::

::: {.fragment}

$=2x(x+2)+3(x+2)$

:::

::: {.fragment}

$=(2x+3)(x+2)$

:::

:::::

::::: {.paper}

::: {.fragment}

<h3>Your turn</h3>

$2x^2-7x+6$

1. Predict the signs.
2. Choose the pair.
3. Split and group on paper.

:::

::: {.fragment}

$P=12$, $S=-7$: both negative.

:::

::: {.fragment}

| Pair | $-1,\ -12$ | $-2,\ -6$ | $-3,\ -4$ |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| Sum | $-13$ | $-8$ | $-7$ |

:::

::: {.fragment}

Choose $-3,-4$: $-3-4=-7$.

:::

::: {.fragment}

$=2x^2-4x-3x+6$

:::

::: {.fragment}

$=2x(x-2)-3(x-2)$

:::

::: {.fragment}

$=(2x-3)(x-2)$

:::

:::::

::::::
